image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey 7-Eleven convenience store building, detailed front elevation with full-width glass frontage and automatic sliding doors under a deep white fascia band carrying the orange green and red horizontal stripe device and the 7-ELEVEN wordmark, backlit lightbox sign and slim canopy edge, interior shelving faintly visible behind the glass, plain rendered side and rear walls with a service door and a small high window, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: white powder-coated aluminium and plate glass at the front, glossy printed lightbox vinyl, flat painted render on the side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique: Fidelity 0.86 -> 0.90. The baked shopfront interior is gone at the user's direction and the feature that scored it is re-scoped to what an exterior shell can deliver; the rectification stays as the ruler and sized the manifestation row it replaced. Two runtime-contract defects fixed: the sign-mount socket shipped as 'socket-0' with its real name buried in userData, and it was parented to building-shell, whose -pi/2 extrude rotation put the declared local (0, 3.54, 3.5) at world (0, 3.5, -3.54) -- on the back wall. Both corrected against the spec, which was right. Front stack re-solved: wall 4.25 -> 4.40, fascia tray 0.92 -> 1.10, head-to-sign gap 0.22 -> 0.34. Side elevation and shell albedos solved through the face's own measured transfer instead of copied from the plate. Gates: turntable PASS with zero holed pixels at every azimuth, check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m, check_part_coverage 0 errors / 0 warnings, all four budget axes inside hero4x. Silhouette IoU 0.568 still fails its 0.85 threshold and the cause is now measured, not asserted: the harness's fixed 35-degree camera rakes the roofline across 0.146 of the frame where the plate's long lens rakes it across 0.018. interiorDifference moved 0.0558 -> 0.0591 over the whole pass, and that is the honest cost of the front stack: an 8x8 mean-colour grid rewards a correctly-sized sign band landing in the plate's cells, and under a different lens a physically correct band cannot. The physical proportion is the right target for a game prop; the pixel layout of one photograph is not.

featureReviews.notes: Up from 0.86. The front wall was raised 4.25 -> 4.40 m with the coping cap sitting ON it (4.40..4.45) rather than inside its last 50 mm, which is also what took check-coplanar back to clean: a cap whose top face shares the wall's top plane is a same-facing pair over 53 m2. Measured at the solved camera (azimuth 34 / elevation 22, re-confirmed here by an elevation sweep -- silhouette aspect 1.713 at el10, 1.570 at el14, 1.458 at el18, 1.370 at el22 against the plate's 1.320, so el22 is the match and nothing lower is): aspectRatioDelta 0.042 -> 0.0296, scaleDelta 0.0017, silhouette IoU 0.507 -> 0.568. Total height 4.59 m (the condenser), inside the 4.60 m module the fourteen shared-module buildings all use. IoU still fails its 0.85 threshold and the reason is now MEASURED rather than asserted: scanning the first foreground row across the frame, the plate's top edge runs y 0.042..0.060 of the silhouette height -- essentially flat -- while the render's runs 0.164..0.018, eight times the convergence. The harness camera is a fixed 35 degree perspective shared by every prop in the kit and by img2threejs's own gates; the plate is a long-lens product render. That is an instrument difference, it is not changeable for one asset, and it caps IoU here.

Up from 0.85. The manifestation decal row is BUILT, at the height and pitch the rectified opening measures (sign/glass.png at 170.7 px/m: the row occupies pixel rows 223-241, i.e. 1.47 m above grade; dashes 0.14 m wide on a 0.27 m pitch, so 22 across the 6.00 m shopfront). It used to be printed into the baked glazing image, which is why an earlier geometry row was dropped -- it landed at 1.20 m and read as a second row beside the printed one. With the image gone there is one row and it is where the plate puts it. Tones are the plate's own, not the brand palette: its tab pixels measure saturation 0.37-0.49 at luma 114-128 against a pane reading 136, so the three are set at brand hue mixed 45% into the pane tone. At full strength they drew a bold dashed line the plate does not have. The head-to-fascia gap opened 0.22 -> 0.34 m (framing top 2.86, tray bottom 3.20). Four bays, centred pair, framed leaves, kickplate and head as before; the row rides in the existing mullion InstancedMesh's material family and costs one draw call and the spec's already-declared decal-tab material, which nothing had ever instantiated.

Up from 0.86. It was a low SLAB: measured off the plate's own roof crop at the unit's depth, apparent height over apparent width is 0.61 and the 1.30 x 0.60 box rendered 0.46. At 1.15 x 0.68 x 0.95 it renders 0.59, without touching the 4.59 m ceiling. The two fans are RECESSED into the flat lid -- a bright rolled rim, a dark throat, a guard -- drawn in the atlas quadrant, where they were two proud cylinders; that is what the plate shows and it removes two lathe rings, so the fix costs negative triangles. The first cut of the recess put ONE fan the size of the whole lid, which is a different machine; there are two at 0.44 of the lid width each. The unit stands on a dark bearer rail rather than four feet. The duct is ONE run with a standing seam and an end cap, where three flange ribs standing 15 mm proud read as a staircase of separate blocks. The coil louvre is now DARK: it had been lifted to luma 130 to clear the turntable's hole test at the backdrop's 58, and the right lever is chroma, not value -- #35485a is luma 68 at saturation 0.41, below the backdrop and nothing like it in chroma. Placement moved from (2.60, 2.20) to (1.60, -1.20): a three-quarter view of a flat roof pushes anything on it toward the near corner, and the unit was crowding the front-right parapet. RESIDUAL, named: the plate and the Meshy proxy both put the parapet at about 0.89 of total height, so the unit should stand roughly twice as proud of the coping as it does. Closing that needs a 5.0 m total, and this asset is one of fourteen sharing an 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 module. The module wins; the shortfall is recorded rather than smoothed over.

Up from 0.84, which had been 'Unchanged' for two passes. The graphic itself was never the problem -- it is the plate's own measured palette and layout with the trademark artwork baked in -- the SIZE was. Column-scanning the coloured stripes in the normalised frame: the plate's band (orange top to red bottom) spans 0.1033 of the silhouette height and the build spanned 0.0783, 24% short. The tray went 0.92 -> 1.10 m and the graphic face 0.80 -> 0.98 m, which takes the band to 0.0950 -- 8% short, and the remainder is what the 4.6 m module leaves between the shopfront head and the coping. The internal proportions were already right and stay right: stripe fractions of the band 0.202 / 0.339 / 0.194 on the plate against 0.193 / 0.325 / 0.193 built.

Up from 0.84. The +X elevation is very nearly MONOCHROME on the plate and the model was painting it like a shopfront. Measured in the normalised frame against a wall at 136.7: leaf 134.2 (0.98 of wall), reveal 93.9 (0.69), window frame 142.3 (1.04), pane 122.5-133.5, lamp 132.1 (0.99), plinth 108.6 (0.79). The leaf carried render-white (albedo 230) and the fittings carried aluminium (188), so once the shell was solved down to its measured grey they stood out as bright white furniture on a grey wall -- the opposite of the plate. Albedos are SOLVED through this face's own transfer R = 0.693 A + 34 rather than copied from the plate, and the grouping follows the tones rather than the parts list: leaf, bulkhead lamp and casement frame all want an albedo within 4% of each other (138 / 137 / 150) so they are one merged geometry on one material, and the reveal is the only genuinely different value (84) so it keeps the fittings mesh. No draw call moved -- both meshes existed. Placement corrected too: the door moved 0.80 m in -Z to sit nearer the middle of the 7.0 m elevation with the casement following by the same 0.80 so the measured gap is kept, and the casement's head is now DERIVED (frame head = door reveal head at 2.31 m) where it used to float half a metre above it.

Up from 0.86, and this is the largest single gain in the pass. The shell albedo was #CFCDC9, chosen by copying the plate's measured tone, and the harness's transfer on this face is affine with a large additive term -- so the elevation the plate makes grey rendered nearly as white as the shopfront surround. Two renders fit it: #CFCDC9 (albedo luma 205) landed at 176, #A9A7A2 (167) landed at 150, giving R = 0.693 A + 34. The plate's side wall reads 135.7 in the same normalised frame, which inverts to albedo luma 147, i.e. #94938E at the plate's hue. Built, it renders 132.8. The side/front luma ratio went 0.83 -> 0.63 against the plate's 0.60. maxDeltaE across the 15 checked component regions moved 12.7 -> 9.0 on the pass where only tones changed; it reads higher on the final frame because the front stack moved and the sampling points ride the spec's declared positions. 13 materials / 16, 18 draw calls / 24, 16 geometries / 32, 1,952 triangles.

REPLACES interior-legibility (0.84), because the brief changed and the old feature scored a thing this prop is no longer allowed to do. The baked interior -- the plate's glazed opening homography-rectified into the shopfront plane and projected by world x/y -- is REMOVED at the user's direction, for the same reason the FamilyMart rebuild never shipped one: a flat photograph on a flat pane has no parallax, so it slides against the framing the moment the camera orbits, and this prop draws its stiles, rails, mullions and header pull as GEOMETRY at the same positions the photograph draws them. The rectification survives as the layout ruler -- it is what the bay, stile, rail and manifestation positions were read off, and it is what sized the decal row in this same pass -- it is simply not a texture. What the feature now measures is whether the pane reads as GLASS rather than as a hole or a painted panel, which is what an exterior shell can actually deliver: turntable_gate reports 0 interior-hole pixels at all four azimuths (the baked version's dark shelving was the thing that had to be lifted 0 -> 100 with a knee at 170 to stay out of the backdrop's band); the pane renders at luma ~175 against a backdrop of 58; roughness 0.08 puts a specular highlight on it that tracks the camera, which is view-dependence a printed reflection cannot have. The only thing printed on it is a 4 x 256 VERTICAL ramp -- sky at the head, the authored tone at eye height, kerb at the cill, endpoints +-11% -- and the axis is the point: it is the same at every bearing, so it has nothing to slide. The side casement does NOT take the ramp; the plate reads it as one flat value, and its albedo is fit on the glazing material itself (126 rendered 92, so 154 lands on the plate's 0.98 of wall) because a pane at roughness 0.08 and metalness 0.10 is specular-dominated and the wall's affine fit does not describe it.
